text: His gray eyes were dull and lifeless, and his face was marked with so many wrinkles that he seemed much older than his years. <break time="0.8s" /> I first heard his story from my grandfather, who had known Murlock well when both of them were living near that great forest. <break time="0.8s" /> One day Murlock was found dead in his cabin, and since it was not a time of coroners and newspapers, people simply agreed that he had died naturally. <break time="0.8s" /> He was buried beside the grave of his wife, who had died so many years before that the settlers remembered almost nothing about her. <break time="0.8s" /> Many years later, as a bold boy, I crept up to the ruined cabin, threw a stone at it, and ran from the ghost that every boy in the area knew haunted the place. <break time="0.8s" /> Long before, when Murlock built his cabin, he was young, strong, and full of hope, and he had brought a young wife with him from the East. <break time="0.8s" /> Her name and character are not recorded, yet she seems to have been a woman worthy of his love, cheerfully sharing the dangers and hardships of his life. <break time="0.8s" /> There is reason to believe that they loved each other deeply, and that the memory of her held Murlock to that lonely place for the rest of his life.
